findings.issue_text: Uncapped limit/offset on the group members endpoint in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb allows any caller (including anonymous users on visible groups) to force full materialization/serialization of a group's entire membership via ?limit=999999999 or force Postgres to walk/sort and discard the entire member set via ?offset=1000000000; clamp both values (e.g., using Discourse's page_params helper) and reject non-positive values

N+1 query shape and unbounded loop in add_members in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb: one SELECT per username plus one join-table INSERT per group.add, all outside a transaction with no cap on usernames, causing ~2M+ round trips for a bulk add of M names; resolve all names with a single User.where(username_lower: list) query, bulk-insert GroupUser rows, and wrap in a transaction

Unbounded serialize-all in admin groups index in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb: Group.order(:name) with no limit is fully serialized (pre-existing, out-of-scope but flagged while the file is open); worth a cap or pagination if custom group counts grow

Phantom empty last page in app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 totalPages: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 produces one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so showingLast fails to disable 'next' on the real last page and clicking it fetches an empty member list; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

P1: Public GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from top-level JSON array to envelope object {members, meta}, breaking external API consumers, plugins, and scripts that iterate the array (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28-35)

P1: PUT/PATCH /admin/groups/:id silently ignores old nested group[name|visible|usernames] payloads and corrupts data — old-format consumers get 200 success while name edits are dropped and group.visible is force-set to false when the param is absent; new-format partial updates (e.g. sending only name) also reset visible (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:35-47)

P1: POST /admin/groups contract changed — flat name/visible params replace group[name|visible|usernames], usernames is never read so groups can no longer be seeded with members at creation, and old-format consumers get group.name = '' leading to 422 validation failure (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:23-33)

P2: Members endpoint now truncates at 50 members for all groups (previously full list for custom groups, 200 for automatic), and the public group members page fetches only 50 with no pagination controls, silently hiding members beyond 50 (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26, routes/group-members.js.es6, templates/group/members.hbs)

P2: create action drops alias_level sent by its own client — the rewritten group.js asJSON() sends alias_level and the form shows the selector for new groups, but create only assigns name and visible, so the chosen alias level is silently lost until a subsequent save (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24-26, models/group.js)

P3: totalPages off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6 — Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields a phantom empty last page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:10-13)

P3: Client model API renamed/reshaped without deprecation — saveWithUsernames → save, createWithUsernames → create, asJSON shape {group: {...}} → flat, and findMembers resolves the raw envelope (returning undefined instead of a promise when name is blank), breaking plugin/custom code calling these methods (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js)

P3: Remove link likely rendered for automatic groups — {{#unless automatic}} in group_member.hbs may resolve against the member/user context instead of the group due to Ember itemView context semantics, rendering the remove '×' for automatic groups; clicking it hits the 422 can_not_modify_automatic guard with no user feedback (app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1)

Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI: the members endpoint applies limit=50 to all groups, but the public members.hbs template and group-members route have no pagination controls, so groups with more than 50 members show an incomplete list with no indication anything is missing

All new async paths have zero error handling: the new Discourse.ajax calls in findMembers/removeMember/addMembers have no failure handlers, routes changed from afterModel returning the findMembers() promise to fire-and-forget setupController calls, and controller removeMember/addMembers actions ignore returned promises — failed loads leave a silently empty list and failed add/remove operations give no user feedback

Off-by-one in totalPages calculation (Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1) produces a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members shows '2' pages); should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit) with a 0 guard

No in-flight guard/sequencing on pagination and mutations: next/previous optimistically set offset and fire findMembers() with no request cancellation, sequence token, or in-flight guard, so rapid clicks or slow responses can resolve out of order and the rendered member list can correspond to a different page than the displayed page number; on failure, offset stays advanced while the list shows the old page

Server members endpoint has unbounded limit with no upper clamp (a client can pass limit=10000000 to force full-group serialization, a repeatable resource-exhaustion vector on a non-admin endpoint), and neither limit nor offset is validated as non-negative — negative values pass into LIMIT/OFFSET -1, which PostgreSQL rejects, producing an unhandled ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid → 500 instead of a 400

PATCH membership API silently no-ops and mutates visible: the request.patch? branch applying incremental changes: {add:, delete:} was removed, so a PATCH to /admin/groups/:id falls into the PUT path, ignores params[:changes], returns success_json, and — because group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" runs unconditionally — sets visible = false when visible is omitted

add_members silently skips unknown usernames and reports success: usernames that don't resolve via User.find_by_username are skipped with no error, and the action returns success_json even if nothing was added, so the admin gets no feedback that a typo'd username was ignored

Spec for the remove_member automatic-group guard uses the wrong HTTP verb: xhr :put, :remove_member hits add_members (which raises on params.require(:usernames)) instead of the DELETE-mapped remove_member action, so the DELETE-path 422 guard for removing members from automatic groups is never actually tested

addMembers client action has no double-submit guard and never clears the input (acknowledged by the '// TODO: should clear the input' comment): repeated clicks re-PUT the same username list, the server has no idempotency guard for already-present members, and any resulting failure is silent

Public groups#members endpoint and frontend findMembers() now limit member lists to 50 with no pagination controls or next/previous actions added to public controllers, silently truncating groups with more than 50 members (regression from previously showing all members, up to 200 for automatic groups)

GroupsController#members response contract rewritten from a serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} with pagination applied to all groups and a changed default limit, with zero spec coverage to verify the shape the frontend findMembers() and other API consumers depend on

Off-by-one in totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 creates a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members with limit 50 shows a page 2/2); Math.ceil is required

Rewritten admin groups create/update actions have thin coverage: the rename path for normal groups, alias_level assignment, visible handling, and the render_json_error validation-failure path are untested because the deleted tests' assertions were not carried over

add_members/remove_member edge cases (silent skip of non-existent users and non-members, usernames.split(',') not stripping whitespace so 'alice, bob' silently skips ' bob', and the newly reachable duplicate-add path) are undocumented and untested after the PATCH tests were deleted

remove_member test uses xhr :put while the route wires delete 'members' to the action, and the new member routes' verb-to-action wiring is never exercised, so a route typo would pass CI; the removed get 'users' route also has no coverage

Tests rely on magic id: 1 / group_id: 1 being an existing automatic group via implicit seed state instead of creating groups with Fabricate(:group, automatic: true) as done elsewhere in the file, making them brittle against seed/schema changes

Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI — limit=50 applied to all groups but pagination controls only added to the admin template, so groups with >50 members show 50 with no way to reach the rest
Off-by-one in totalPages calculation (Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1) produces an empty trailing page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)
add_members silently ignores unknown usernames and reports success — User.find_by_username has no else branch, so misspelled/nonexistent usernames are dropped while success_json is still rendered

create action drops alias_level that the form collects — client sends alias_level in asJSON() and the new-group form renders the alias combo-box, but create only assigns name and visible, so the alias level is silently lost until a subsequent save

update unconditionally overwrites visible and compares against a string — group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" runs even when the param is absent, flipping groups to invisible on partial updates, and a JSON boolean true fails the string comparison
add_members assumes usernames is a String — params.require(:usernames).split(",") raises NoMethodError resulting in a 500 if a JSON API client posts an array
findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise on the empty-name path — the old code returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), creating a mixed contract that breaks any caller chaining .then on the result

remove_member bypasses the model's domain API — removal switched from group.remove(user) to a raw group.users.delete(user_id), diverging from group.add(user) and potentially skipping side effects encapsulated in Group#remove

Pagination logic duplicated across three layers — page math recomputed client-side despite server returning meta.total/limit/offset, and offset clamping exists in both controller actions and the model, creating drift risk
Public members endpoint doesn't validate offset/limit — params[:offset].to_i accepts negatives causing OFFSET -1 SQL error and 500 on a public endpoint, and limit is unbounded
addMembers never clears the selector after adding — usernames keeps its value so a second click re-submits the same names, leaving the add-members flow with no feedback loop

Public group member list silently truncated to 50 with no pagination: server applies limit=50 to all groups (previously non-automatic groups rendered the entire member list), and the public route/template have no page state or pagination UI, so users see 50 rows of larger groups with no indication anything is missing

totalPages off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members / 50 limit gives totalPages=2); should use Math.ceil, otherwise 'next' stays enabled and clicking it lands the admin on an empty page

Remove control renders for automatic groups: {{#unless automatic}} in group_member.hbs is evaluated in the member's context (a Discourse.User) where automatic is undefined, so the remove link shows for every member of automatic groups; clicking it triggers a DELETE that returns 422, and the rejected promise from model.removeMember is unhandled, producing a confirmation dialog followed by a silent no-op

Stale usernames carried across groups: usernames is a plain controller property on the reused adminGroup controller and setupController never resets it, so pending usernames typed for group A persist when navigating to group B and clicking 'Add' inserts them into the wrong group; addMembers also never clears the input after a successful add, so a second click re-submits the same list

Admin groups #update breaks the existing PUT/PATCH contract: the action reads only flat params while old clients sent group[name]/group[visible]/group[usernames] and changes[add]/changes[delete]; for old-format callers, params[:visible] is nil so group.visible is silently set to false, membership changes are silently ignored, and the action still returns success_json (200)

Unbounded limit on the public members endpoint: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no ceiling (old code capped automatic groups at 200), so limit=1000000 serializes the full membership of any visible group in one request — a mass user enumeration and DoS vector; also offset=-1 passes straight through to SQL (OFFSET -1) causing a 500

remove_member bypasses association callbacks: group.users.delete(user_id) issues a raw delete on the group_users join table, skipping GroupUser callbacks and whatever maintains the cached user_count column (adds go through group.add but removals have no equivalent); the trailing group.save saves an unchanged record and recomputes nothing, so member counts can be stale/inflated after removals

add_members succeeds silently when nothing was added: unknown usernames are silently skipped and the 'if group.save' guard always passes since saving an unmodified group can't fail, so the endpoint returns success_json even when zero users were added and the admin UI shows no feedback for a typo'd username

Removing the last member of the final page strands the UI on an empty page: after a successful removal, findMembers() re-fetches with the unchanged offset, so if the removed member was the only one on the last page the refetch returns an empty list and the admin is left on an empty page until manually clicking previous; offset should be re-clamped against the new total after deletion

Pagination race in admin-group next/previous: each click computes offset from current model state and fires an unguarded findMembers whose response overwrites offset, user_count, and members in completion order; rapid clicks can issue duplicate requests (model offset isn't updated until the response arrives) and out-of-order responses leave the UI showing a page other than the one last clicked

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Uncapped limit/offset on the group members endpoint in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb allows any caller (including anonymous users on visible groups) to force full materialization/serialization of a group's entire membership via ?limit=999999999 or force Postgres to walk/sort and discard the entire member set via ?offset=1000000000; clamp both values (e.g., using Discourse's page_params helper) and reject non-positive values

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces client-controlled pagination for *all* groups: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, which are then passed directly into `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serialized. There is no clamping/validation of `limit` or `offset` (e.g., max page size, non-negative/non-zero), so a caller can request extremely large limits or offsets, potentially causing expensive DB work and large serialization responses. This was previously only applied to `automatic?` groups; the change expands the attack surface to all visible groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query shape and unbounded loop in add_members in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb: one SELECT per username plus one join-table INSERT per group.add, all outside a transaction with no cap on usernames, causing ~2M+ round trips for a bulk add of M names; resolve all names with a single User.where(username_lower: list) query, bulk-insert GroupUser rows, and wrap in a transaction

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each` with `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop and `group.add(user)` per user, followed by `group.save` (no transaction, no cap/validation on how many usernames can be submitted). This creates an N+1 query/insert pattern and potentially unbounded work for large input, which is a concrete performance/scalability concern grounded in the added code, though not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded serialize-all in admin groups index in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb: Group.order(:name) with no limit is fully serialized (pre-existing, out-of-scope but flagged while the file is open); worth a cap or pagination if custom group counts grow

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#index the code still does `groups = Group.order(:name)` and then `render_serialized(groups, BasicGroupSerializer)` with only optional filtering (`search`, `ignore_automatic`) and no `limit`/pagination. From the diff, this will serialize all matching groups, which is a potential scalability/performance concern (especially for large group counts), but not a functional defect shown as introduced by this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Phantom empty last page in app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 totalPages: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 produces one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so showingLast fails to disable 'next' on the real last page and clicking it fetches an empty member list; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 creates an extra page when user_count is exactly divisible by limit, allowing navigation to an empty last page, and suggests using Math.ceil instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Public GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from top-level JSON array to envelope object {members, meta}, breaking external API consumers, plugins, and scripts that iterate the array (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28-35)

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns a top-level JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e., an envelope object. Any existing consumers expecting an array from GET /groups/:name/members will break unless updated, and the diff shows this is a behavioral/API contract change rather than a purely internal refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: PUT/PATCH /admin/groups/:id silently ignores old nested group[name|visible|usernames] payloads and corrupts data — old-format consumers get 200 success while name edits are dropped and group.visible is force-set to false when the param is absent; new-format partial updates (e.g. sending only name) also reset visible (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:35-47)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff replaces the old nested payload handling (`payload = params[:group]` with `payload[:name]`, `payload[:visible]`, etc.) with top-level params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`). As written, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will force `visible` to `false` whenever `visible` is omitted (e.g., partial updates or old clients still sending `group: { visible: ... }`). Old-format consumers sending `group[name|visible|usernames]` will have those ignored, yet can still get `200` if the record saves, leading to silent dropped updates and potential unintended `visible=false` changes. This is directly shown in `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb` update logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: POST /admin/groups contract changed — flat name/visible params replace group[name|visible|usernames], usernames is never read so groups can no longer be seeded with members at creation, and old-format consumers get group.name = '' leading to 422 validation failure (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:23-33)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#create to read flat params (params[:name], params[:visible]) and no longer reads params[:group] or usernames (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb create). Previously create accepted params[:group][:name] and params[:group][:usernames]. With the new code, old-format clients sending group[name]/group[visible]/group[usernames] will result in name being set to '' (since params[:name] is nil), causing group.save to fail if name is required. Also, usernames are not processed on create anymore, so creating a group with initial members via POST /admin/groups is no longer possible in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Members endpoint now truncates at 50 members for all groups (previously full list for custom groups, 200 for automatic), and the public group members page fetches only 50 with no pagination controls, silently hiding members beyond 50 (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26, routes/group-members.js.es6, templates/group/members.hbs)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination with a default `limit` of 50 for *all* groups (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`), whereas previously only automatic groups were limited (default 200) and non-automatic groups returned the full list. On the public group members route, `routes/group-members.js.es6` now sets `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();` and the template `group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}`, relying on the model’s `members` property populated by `findMembers()`. There are no pagination controls added to the public `group/members.hbs`, so only the first 50 members will be shown with no way to navigate to later pages, effectively hiding members beyond 50.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: create action drops alias_level sent by its own client — the rewritten group.js asJSON() sends alias_level and the form shows the selector for new groups, but create only assigns name and visible, so the chosen alias level is silently lost until a subsequent save (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24-26, models/group.js)

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: client now POSTs alias_level for new groups (Discourse.Group#asJSON returns {name, alias_level, visible} and create() sends data: this.asJSON()), and the new-group form still renders the alias_level combo-box. But Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible (no alias_level), so the chosen alias level is ignored/lost on creation until a later update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: totalPages off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6 — Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields a phantom empty last page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:10-13)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (lines ~10-13 in the added code). When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50), this returns 3 instead of 2, creating a phantom empty last page. The diff also shows `next` can set `offset` up to `user_count`, and `findMembers` allows `offset == user_count`, which would fetch an empty page consistent with this off-by-one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Client model API renamed/reshaped without deprecation — saveWithUsernames → save, createWithUsernames → create, asJSON shape {group: {...}} → flat, and findMembers resolves the raw envelope (returning undefined instead of a promise when name is blank), breaking plugin/custom code calling these methods (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js)

P3: Remove link likely rendered for automatic groups — {{#unless automatic}} in group_member.hbs may resolve against the member/user context instead of the group due to Ember itemView context semantics, rendering the remove '×' for automatic groups; clicking it hits the 422 can_not_modify_automatic guard with no user feedback (app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1)

adjudication.rationale: In `group.hbs`, members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, meaning `group_member.hbs` is evaluated in the per-`member` item view context. The template uses `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}`, but `automatic` is a property of the group/model, not of an individual member (`Discourse.User`). With `automatic` likely undefined in the member context, the `unless` will evaluate truthy and render the remove “×” link even for automatic groups. Clicking it triggers `removeMember` which calls `model.removeMember` and will get a 422 from `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` for automatic groups, with no UI feedback shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI: the members endpoint applies limit=50 to all groups, but the public members.hbs template and group-members route have no pagination controls, so groups with more than 50 members show an incomplete list with no indication anything is missing

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for *all* groups, whereas previously only automatic groups were limited (and others returned the full list). On the client, the public group members route now just calls `model.findMembers()` (which uses the model default `limit: 50, offset: 0`) and the `group/members.hbs` template simply iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination controls added in this diff. This will show only the first 50 members with no UI to navigate or indicate more exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All new async paths have zero error handling: the new Discourse.ajax calls in findMembers/removeMember/addMembers have no failure handlers, routes changed from afterModel returning the findMembers() promise to fire-and-forget setupController calls, and controller removeMember/addMembers actions ignore returned promises — failed loads leave a silently empty list and failed add/remove operations give no user feedback
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that the route changed from returning the findMembers() promise (afterModel) to a fire-and-forget call in setupController, meaning the async findMembers load is not awaited/handled. This implies the controller may render before member data is available (race condition), which is the golden issue (plus additional error-handling concerns).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages calculation (Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1) produces a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members shows '2' pages); should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit) with a 0 guard

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` with only a `user_count == 0` guard. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50/50), this returns 2 instead of 1, enabling navigation to an extra empty page. This is reinforced by `next` setting `offset` up to `user_count` and `findMembers` requesting `/members.json` with that offset, which will return an empty `members` list for `offset == total`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No in-flight guard/sequencing on pagination and mutations: next/previous optimistically set offset and fire findMembers() with no request cancellation, sequence token, or in-flight guard, so rapid clicks or slow responses can resolve out of order and the rendered member list can correspond to a different page than the displayed page number; on failure, offset stays advanced while the list shows the old page

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `next`/`previous` actions immediately mutate `model.offset` and then call `group.findMembers()` with no in-flight guard or request sequencing. `findMembers` issues an async `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` and unconditionally `setProperties({ offset: result.meta.offset, members: ... })` on resolution. With rapid clicks or slow/out-of-order responses, an earlier request can resolve after a later one and overwrite `offset/members` with stale page data, effectively showing a different page than the user’s last action. Additionally, there’s no error handling; on failure the optimistic `offset` change remains while `members` stays from the prior page, creating a page-number/list mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server members endpoint has unbounded limit with no upper clamp (a client can pass limit=10000000 to force full-group serialization, a repeatable resource-exhaustion vector on a non-admin endpoint), and neither limit nor offset is validated as non-negative — negative values pass into LIMIT/OFFSET -1, which PostgreSQL rejects, producing an unhandled ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid → 500 instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale:
In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination params are taken directly from the request: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then used in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or non-negative validation. This allows a client to request an arbitrarily large `limit` (potential resource exhaustion due to large query + serialization) and to pass negative `limit/offset` values, which can cause an `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid`/DB error and a 500 since the action doesn’t handle/translate it into a 400.

Relevant diff: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb` members action changes to always apply `limit/offset` and return JSON meta, but adds no clamping/validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH membership API silently no-ops and mutates visible: the request.patch? branch applying incremental changes: {add:, delete:} was removed, so a PATCH to /admin/groups/:id falls into the PUT path, ignores params[:changes], returns success_json, and — because group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" runs unconditionally — sets visible = false when visible is omitted

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController`, the previous `update` method handled `request.patch?` via `update_patch(group)` to apply `params[:changes]` (incremental membership add/delete). That branch (and `update_patch`) was removed; `update` now always runs the PUT-style logic and never reads `params[:changes]`, so a PATCH request will silently ignore `{add:, delete:}`. Additionally, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is executed unconditionally in the new `update`, so if a PATCH omits `visible`, it will be set to `false` (since `nil == "true"` is false). This matches the reported behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unknown usernames and reports success: usernames that don't resolve via User.find_by_username are skipped with no error, and the action returns success_json even if nothing was added, so the admin gets no feedback that a typo'd username was ignored

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown usernames are simply skipped (`if user = ...`). It then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if no users were added. This matches the finding (no feedback for typos), but it’s more of a UX/API design concern than a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec for the remove_member automatic-group guard uses the wrong HTTP verb: xhr :put, :remove_member hits add_members (which raises on params.require(:usernames)) instead of the DELETE-mapped remove_member action, so the DELETE-path 422 guard for removing members from automatic groups is never actually tested
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both identify that the remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb (PUT via xhr :put) while the route/action expects DELETE, meaning the intended remove_member DELETE path isn’t actually being exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers client action has no double-submit guard and never clears the input (acknowledged by the '// TODO: should clear the input' comment): repeated clicks re-PUT the same username list, the server has no idempotency guard for already-present members, and any resulting failure is silent

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not clear `this.usernames` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(...)`. The add button in `group.hbs` also has no `disabled` binding/guard, so repeated clicks will re-issue the same PUT. Additionally, `addMembers` does not `return`/handle the promise from `model.addMembers` (no `.then`/error handling), so any server error (e.g. 422 for automatic groups) would not be surfaced here. However, the claim that the server has no idempotency guard for already-present members / that duplicates will result is not verifiable from this diff because `group.add(user)` may already be idempotent at the model/DB level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public groups#members endpoint and frontend findMembers() now limit member lists to 50 with no pagination controls or next/previous actions added to public controllers, silently truncating groups with more than 50 members (regression from previously showing all members, up to 200 for automatic groups)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, returning only `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` (no special-casing for non-automatic groups anymore). On the frontend, the public `group-members` route now calls `model.findMembers()` and the `group/members.hbs` template iterates `{{#each m in members}}`, i.e., it will only render `model.members` populated by `findMembers()`. Unlike the admin group UI, there are no next/previous actions or pagination controls added for the public group members page in this diff, so groups with >50 members will show only the first 50 with no way to navigate—silent truncation/regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#members response contract rewritten from a serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} with pagination applied to all groups and a changed default limit, with zero spec coverage to verify the shape the frontend findMembers() and other API consumers depend on

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` to a JSON object with `members:` plus `meta: { total, limit, offset }`, and applies `limit`/`offset` pagination to all groups with a new default `limit` of 50 (`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`). The frontend `Discourse.Group#findMembers()` was updated to consume this new shape (`result.members` and `result.meta.*`), but there is no spec added/updated for `GroupsController#members` to lock down this response contract (only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` changes are present). This is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern about untested API contract and pagination behavior, even if the immediate Ember consumer was updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 creates a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members with limit 50 shows a page 2/2); Math.ceil is required

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` when `user_count > 0`. If `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50/50), this returns 2 instead of 1, creating an extra empty page. This is reinforced by the `next` action allowing `offset` to become `user_count` (via `Math.min(..., group.get("user_count"))`), and `findMembers` then requests `offset = user_count`, which will return an empty `members` list. Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and clamping offset to `user_count - limit` max) would avoid the phantom page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rewritten admin groups create/update actions have thin coverage: the rename path for normal groups, alias_level assignment, visible handling, and the render_json_error validation-failure path are untested because the deleted tests' assertions were not carried over

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites `Admin::GroupsController#create` and `#update` to accept top-level params (`name`, `visible`, `alias_level`) and changes behavior (e.g., `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if ...`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, `group.name = params[:name] if ... && !group.automatic`). In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, new tests cover name stripping on create and ignoring renames for automatic groups, plus add/remove members endpoints, but there is no test for (a) renaming a *non-automatic* group, (b) alias_level assignment on update, (c) visible handling beyond the automatic-group case, or (d) the `render_json_error` paths when `group.save` fails in create/update/add_members/remove_member. These are specific, newly/reworked code paths with no corresponding assertions carried over from deleted tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members/remove_member edge cases (silent skip of non-existent users and non-members, usernames.split(',') not stripping whitespace so 'alice, bob' silently skips ' bob', and the newly reachable duplicate-add path) are undocumented and untested after the PATCH tests were deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the old PATCH-based membership changes (and deletes the incremental PATCH specs) with new endpoints `add_members`/`remove_member` in `Admin::GroupsController`. In `add_members`, `usernames.split(",").each` does not strip whitespace and silently ignores unknown usernames (`User.find_by_username` nil), so inputs like "alice, bob" will likely skip " bob". In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` will silently no-op if the user isn’t a member. The updated specs add only happy-path tests for adding/removing and an automatic-group restriction, but do not cover these edge cases, leaving previously-covered behavior (via the deleted PATCH tests) untested for the new code paths. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test/edge-case gap rather than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member test uses xhr :put while the route wires delete 'members' to the action, and the new member routes' verb-to-action wiring is never exercised, so a route typo would pass CI; the removed get 'users' route also has no coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under `context ".remove_member"`, the first test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, while `config/routes.rb` wires `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`). Controller specs invoke the action directly and don’t verify route verb/path wiring, so this mismatch wouldn’t catch a routing typo; likewise the removed `get "users"` route has no route-level coverage in this diff. This is a specific test/coverage gap rather than a runtime defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests rely on magic id: 1 / group_id: 1 being an existing automatic group via implicit seed state instead of creating groups with Fabricate(:group, automatic: true) as done elsewhere in the file, making them brittle against seed/schema changes

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb several new tests hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` to represent an automatic group (e.g. `.update` "ignore name change on automatic group", `.add_members` "cannot add members to automatic groups", `.remove_member` "cannot remove members from automatic groups"). The diff does not fabricate an automatic group with that id in these examples, so the tests implicitly depend on seeded/fixture state (e.g. a built-in automatic group having id 1). This makes the tests brittle to seed/schema/order changes; other tests in the file correctly use `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI — limit=50 applied to all groups but pagination controls only added to the admin template, so groups with >50 members show 50 with no way to reach the rest

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` for all groups (previously the limit/offset logic only applied to `group.automatic?`). On the client, `Discourse.Group` now has `limit: 50` and `findMembers()` requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with that limit/offset, and the public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders `{{#each m in members}}` without adding any pagination controls. Pagination UI/actions (`next`/`previous`, page counts) were only added to the *admin* group template/controller. Therefore the public members page will show only the first 50 members with no way (in this diff) to reach subsequent pages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages calculation (Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1) produces an empty trailing page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)
add_members silently ignores unknown usernames and reports success — User.find_by_username has no else branch, so misspelled/nonexistent usernames are dropped while success_json is still rendered

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are iterated and only added when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown usernames are simply skipped (`if user = ...` with no else). After the loop it still renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, so misspelled/nonexistent usernames can be dropped without any error/feedback. This behavior also existed previously in the removed `update_patch` logic (which even had a spec asserting silent success), so it’s not clearly a newly introduced correctness defect, but it is a real, diff-grounded behavioral concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create action drops alias_level that the form collects — client sends alias_level in asJSON() and the new-group form renders the alias combo-box, but create only assigns name and visible, so the alias level is silently lost until a subsequent save

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: client `Discourse.Group.asJSON()` includes `alias_level` and `create()` POSTs `{ name, alias_level, visible }` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js). The new-group form still renders and binds `{{combo-box ... value=alias_level ...}}` (admin/templates/group.hbs). But server `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads `params[:alias_level]` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb), so the selected alias level is ignored on create until a later update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update unconditionally overwrites visible and compares against a string — group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" runs even when the param is absent, flipping groups to invisible on partial updates, and a JSON boolean true fails the string comparison

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff shows `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` executed unconditionally, unlike `alias_level` which is guarded by `if params[:alias_level].present?`. If `visible` is omitted, `params[:visible]` is `nil` and the expression becomes `false`, overwriting the persisted value and potentially flipping a group to invisible on a partial update. Also, the code compares to the string "true", so a boolean `true` (e.g., if sent as JSON) would not match and would also set `visible` to `false`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members assumes usernames is a String — params.require(:usernames).split(",") raises NoMethodError resulting in a 500 if a JSON API client posts an array

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff sets `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If a client submits `usernames` as an Array (e.g., JSON `{"usernames":["a","b"]}`), `split` is undefined and would raise `NoMethodError`, causing a 500. The diff introduces this new endpoint and parsing logic without guarding/coercing the type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise on the empty-name path — the old code returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), creating a mixed contract that breaks any caller chaining .then on the result
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: there is a code path in the function (e.g., empty-name path) that does not explicitly return a value, causing it to return undefined. The candidate adds context that callers expect a Promise (previously Ember.RSVP.resolve([])), but the core issue matches the golden comment about missing returns leading to undefined.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member bypasses the model's domain API — removal switched from group.remove(user) to a raw group.users.delete(user_id), diverging from group.add(user) and potentially skipping side effects encapsulated in Group#remove

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the diff switches to `group.users.delete(user_id)` (raw association mutation) whereas other membership changes in this diff use the Group domain API (`group.add(user)` in add_members) and the previous implementation used `group.remove(user)` in update_patch. The diff doesn’t show what `Group#remove` does, so we can’t verify skipped side effects as an actual bug, but the inconsistency and potential bypass of encapsulated behavior is a concrete, diff-grounded design/maintenance concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination logic duplicated across three layers — page math recomputed client-side despite server returning meta.total/limit/offset, and offset clamping exists in both controller actions and the model, creating drift risk

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows pagination/offset logic implemented in multiple client-side places: the admin controller actions `next`/`previous` clamp offsets with `Math.min(..., user_count)` / `Math.max(..., 0)` before calling `group.findMembers()`, while `Discourse.Group.findMembers` also clamps with `Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))`. The server `GroupsController#members` returns `meta: { total, limit, offset }`, but the client still derives `currentPage`/`totalPages` from `offset/limit/user_count` rather than consuming any server-provided paging abstraction. This is a real maintainability/architecture concern (risk of drift if formulas or bounds change), but not a directly verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint doesn't validate offset/limit — params[:offset].to_i accepts negatives causing OFFSET -1 SQL error and 500 on a public endpoint, and limit is unbounded

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff now does `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and directly applies them to the query: `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping/validation, so a negative `offset` (e.g. `-1`) can be passed through to SQL `OFFSET -1`, which can raise an error and yield a 500 on this public endpoint. Additionally, `limit` is user-controlled and unbounded (can be set arbitrarily large), which can cause performance/DoS issues. This behavior is visible and grounded in the changed controller code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers never clears the selector after adding — usernames keeps its value so a second click re-submits the same names, leaving the add-members flow with no feedback loop

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not reset `this.get("usernames")` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))`. Since the `user-selector` is bound to `usernames` in `group.hbs`, the entered value will persist and a second click will resend the same usernames. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/flow issue, but it’s not clearly a correctness defect because the server-side add is likely idempotent (adding existing members again) and nothing in the diff shows a hard failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group member list silently truncated to 50 with no pagination: server applies limit=50 to all groups (previously non-automatic groups rendered the entire member list), and the public route/template have no page state or pagination UI, so users see 50 rows of larger groups with no indication anything is missing

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public `/groups/:id/members` endpoint to always paginate: `GroupsController#members` now applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for all groups, whereas previously only automatic groups were limited and non-automatic groups returned the full list. On the client side, the public route `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now sets the model to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` defaults to `limit: 50, offset: 0` and loads only one page into `members`. The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}` but there is no pagination UI/state/actions added for the public members page (pagination controls were only added to the admin template/controller). Result: public group member list will show only the first 50 members with no indication or way to navigate, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members / 50 limit gives totalPages=2); should use Math.ceil, otherwise 'next' stays enabled and clicking it lands the admin on an empty page
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same pagination edge case: when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, the logic allows navigation to a non-existent extra page, resulting in an empty member list on the last/next page. The golden frames it as capping next offset at user_count (offset==total), while the candidate frames it as totalPages off-by-one (Math.floor+1) keeping 'next' enabled, but the underlying bug/UX outcome is the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Remove control renders for automatic groups: {{#unless automatic}} in group_member.hbs is evaluated in the member's context (a Discourse.User) where automatic is undefined, so the remove link shows for every member of automatic groups; clicking it triggers a DELETE that returns 422, and the rejected promise from model.removeMember is unhandled, producing a confirmation dialog followed by a silent no-op

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs`, members are rendered as `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, so the `group-member` view/template runs in the *member* (a `Discourse.User`) context. In `admin/templates/group_member.hbs`, `{{#unless automatic}}...remove...{{/unless}}` therefore checks `automatic` on the user, where it is undefined/falsy, causing the remove link to render even for automatic groups. Clicking it triggers `actions.removeMember` in `admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6`, which calls `model.removeMember(member)`; on automatic groups the server returns 422 (`Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` calls `can_not_modify_automatic`), and the returned rejected promise is not handled in the action, matching the finding’s described behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale usernames carried across groups: usernames is a plain controller property on the reused adminGroup controller and setupController never resets it, so pending usernames typed for group A persist when navigating to group B and clicking 'Add' inserts them into the wrong group; addMembers also never clears the input after a successful add, so a second click re-submits the same list

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `usernames` a plain mutable controller property (`usernames: null` in `admin-group.js.es6`) and `AdminGroupRoute#setupController` now only sets `model` and calls `model.findMembers()` without resetting `controller.usernames` (it used to set other state like `members`). Since Ember routes typically reuse a single controller instance, a typed `usernames` value can persist when switching between different groups, and `actions.addMembers` submits `this.get("usernames")` to the *current* model without clearing it (there’s even a `// TODO: should clear the input`). This can lead to accidentally adding the previous group’s pending usernames to the next group and allows repeated re-submission on multiple clicks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin groups #update breaks the existing PUT/PATCH contract: the action reads only flat params while old clients sent group[name]/group[visible]/group[usernames] and changes[add]/changes[delete]; for old-format callers, params[:visible] is nil so group.visible is silently set to false, membership changes are silently ignored, and the action still returns success_json (200)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#update to only read flat params (params[:alias_level], params[:visible], params[:name]) and removes the prior PATCH handling (changes[add]/changes[delete]) and the PUT payload under params[:group]. In the new code, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will set `visible` to false when old clients send `group[visible]` (so params[:visible] is nil), and membership updates sent via PATCH/changes are no longer applied at all. The action can still return `success_json` (200) if the save succeeds, masking the ignored inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded limit on the public members endpoint: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no ceiling (old code capped automatic groups at 200), so limit=1000000 serializes the full membership of any visible group in one request — a mass user enumeration and DoS vector; also offset=-1 passes straight through to SQL (OFFSET -1) causing a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces user-controlled pagination params applied to all groups without any bounding/sanitization: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no max cap on `limit`, so a request can ask for an extremely large page size, leading to very large DB work and response serialization (DoS/user enumeration risk) in a single request. `offset` is also not clamped to >= 0, so negative values are passed directly into the query via `.offset(offset)`, which can error depending on the DB/ORM behavior. (Note: the finding’s claim that the old code “capped automatic groups at 200” isn’t accurate because it still accepted `params[:limit]`, but the lack of a ceiling/offset validation in the new code is verifiable in the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member bypasses association callbacks: group.users.delete(user_id) issues a raw delete on the group_users join table, skipping GroupUser callbacks and whatever maintains the cached user_count column (adds go through group.add but removals have no equivalent); the trailing group.save saves an unchanged record and recomputes nothing, so member counts can be stale/inflated after removals

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the diff replaces the prior membership-removal path (previously `group.remove(user)` in update_patch) with `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then `group.save`. For a has_many/through association, `delete` removes the join row directly (no join-model callbacks), unlike the existing add path which calls `group.add(user)`. Since `group.save` doesn’t change any Group attributes here, it won’t inherently fix any counter/cache maintenance that would normally run via the association remove/callback path, so cached/denormalized counts like `user_count` can become stale after removals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members succeeds silently when nothing was added: unknown usernames are silently skipped and the 'if group.save' guard always passes since saving an unmodified group can't fail, so the endpoint returns success_json even when zero users were added and the admin UI shows no feedback for a typo'd username

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, unknown usernames are explicitly ignored (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), and the action returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` returns truthy—there’s no check that any users were actually added. The Ember action `addMembers` also doesn’t handle/display any server-side “nothing added” feedback; it just calls `model.addMembers(...)` and reloads members. However, this “silent skip” behavior appears consistent with the prior implementation (the removed spec previously asserted silent success when adding non-existent users), so it’s a real UX/behavior concern but not a clearly unintended defect based solely on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the last member of the final page strands the UI on an empty page: after a successful removal, findMembers() re-fetches with the unchanged offset, so if the removed member was the only one on the last page the refetch returns an empty list and the admin is left on an empty page until manually clicking previous; offset should be re-clamped against the new total after deletion

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#removeMember`, after a successful DELETE it calls `self.findMembers()` without changing `offset` (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`). `findMembers()` clamps the request offset using the *current* `this.get("user_count")` (pre-deletion) and the current `this.get("offset")`, then sends that offset to `/groups/:name/members.json` (`offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`). The server endpoint `GroupsController#members` does not re-clamp `offset` against the new total (it just uses `offset = params[:offset].to_i`), so if you delete the only member on the last page (e.g., total goes from 51 to 50 with limit 50, offset remains 50), the refetch returns an empty `members` array and the UI stays on an empty page until the user clicks previous.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination race in admin-group next/previous: each click computes offset from current model state and fires an unguarded findMembers whose response overwrites offset, user_count, and members in completion order; rapid clicks can issue duplicate requests (model offset isn't updated until the response arrives) and out-of-order responses leave the UI showing a page other than the one last clicked

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `next`/`previous` actions update `group.offset` and then call `group.findMembers()` without canceling/serializing in-flight requests. In `discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers()` issues an AJAX request and then `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` from the response (`result.meta.*`). If multiple clicks trigger multiple `findMembers()` calls, responses can resolve out of order and an older response will overwrite `members` and `offset` to an earlier page, leaving the UI showing a page other than the last click. (The finding’s sub-claim that offset isn’t updated until the response arrives is incorrect, since `group.set("offset", offset)` happens before the request, but the out-of-order overwrite is still real.)
